approach: Add one reading-acceptance check, `check_outcome_state(reading, request, attempt)`, in `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`. It runs as a `step!` line in `refusing_check`, directly after `check_governance_coverage`. It applies only when the reading has a capability, no question and at least one deliverable. It looks for a delivery verb (publish, deploy, share, release) in the request. A retry's earlier request counts too, so a "try again" complaint cannot hide the verb. If a verb is found, the check requires an acceptance criterion that names an observable state: a URL (`http://` or `https://` also count), reachable, served, live at, downloadable, installable, tag, published release or visible to. The one other way out is an `out_of_scope` item that names the verb. Otherwise it refuses, and the refusal text says which state words to add. The verb counts only when it starts a sentence, line or bullet. A leading `-`, `*`, `1.`, `1)` or `(a)` is skipped. So the imperative use ("Publish a first explainer page...") is caught, while the mid-sentence use in this job's own request ("verbs like publish, deploy or share") and a noun use ("Release notes", "Share of") are not. The refusal reaches the reader through the existing one-re-read path in `Athena::read_for` (reading.rs:663-671), so `READING_RULES` and the 3-token headroom in `briefs.rs` are not touched. Existing tests and one corpus case that use publish/deploy requests with file-only criteria are updated to add a state criterion. New unit tests, new corpus cases, a CHANGELOG entry and a decisions entry are added.

decisions.choice: Fix it as a `step!` check in `refusing_check`, in the reading-acceptance gate, and not in the reader prompt or `READING_RULES`.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a request is accepted as a reading with no comparison to the state the user observes. A step! check is mechanical and the corpus test forces a refusing case for it. `briefs.rs` has 3 tokens of headroom and a test asserting exactly 6 rules. The refusal text reaches the reader through `read_for`'s one re-read (reading.rs:663-671).

rejected.option: Add a seventh rule to READING_RULES in briefs.rs
rejected.why: The test asserts exactly 6 rules and the reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom. Prose in a prompt is also not enforced by mechanism.

rejected.option: A project glossary of terms loaded into every reading step (introspection d7s1)
rejected.why: It is a content project (ontology work) that job 20261017-173508-0wtc already failed on. It does not check the reading against the observable state, and it is out of scope here.

rejected.option: Fix the three jobs' own outputs (Pages workflow, site task, ontology file)
rejected.why: That fixes instances. The root cause is that acceptance never compares a delivery verb with an observable state.

decisions.choice: Place the new `step!` directly after `check_governance_coverage`, before the boundary and repo-file checks. It is after `check_criteria_evidence`, as the reading asks.
decisions.reason: Existing tests that expect the governance error for 'Publish to GitHub Pages from .github/workflows/pages.yml' keep their order. For example, the `bare` case at reading.rs:7083 and the retry test at reading.rs:7247-7256 expect the governance message. The governance refusal is the more specific repair.

rejected.why: It would pre-empt the governance refusal in the existing order-sensitive tests and change which message the reader sees first, for no gain.
A reading would pass the path checks only to be refused afterwards, and nothing is gained over the chosen slot.

decisions.choice: A delivery verb counts only when it begins a sentence, line or bullet (after `-`, `*`, `1.`, `1)` or `(a)`, split on newline and . ! ? : ;). It does not count when the next word is `of`, `notes`, `note`, `process`, `workflow`, `checklist`, `candidate` or `cycle`. The scan covers `request` and, for a retry, `attempt.request`.
decisions.reason: It matches the imperative that sets the goal ('Publish a first explainer page...', 'Deploy the site on every push') and keeps the false-refusal rate low. This job's own request names the verbs mid-sentence and must still be accepted. 'Release notes' and 'Share of' are noun uses. A retry's own text is a complaint ('Try again'), so the earlier request is the only place the verb survives. `EarlierAttempt.request` exists (corpus `earlier()` builds it).

rejected.option: Match the four words anywhere in the request as whole words
rejected.why: It would refuse any request that mentions a release, a share or a deployment in passing, including this job's own request, and is a high false-refusal risk.

rejected.option: Scan the reading's title and summary as well
rejected.why: The reader writes those words, so they are a weaker signal and risk refusing the reader's own wording. The request is what the user said.

decisions.choice: Accept state words from a small fixed list matched as whole phrases on lowercased, whitespace-normalised criterion text of any kind: url, urls, reachable, reachability, served, serves, live at, downloadable, installable, tag, published release, visible to; plus the substrings `http://` and `https://`. An `out_of_scope` item containing the verb's stem (e.g. publish, deploy, share, release, so 'deployment' counts) also satisfies the check.
decisions.reason: The list matches the reading's stated words. The out_of_scope exit lets a reading say plainly that the job does not publish, which the user then sees at acceptance, as `governance_is_covered` does for governance files.

rejected.option: Require a behavior-kind criterion that fetches the URL
rejected.why: The verifier may run no network command, so most such criteria could never be demonstrated. The check requires that the state is named, not that it is fetched.
More words mean more false accepts. The list is kept small and conservative on purpose.

decisions.choice: Update the existing tests and the one corpus case whose request begins with a delivery verb. Give their readings a criterion that names a reachable URL, instead of weakening the check.

rejected.option: Skip the check when the request names a governance path or a brand word
rejected.why: 'Publish to GitHub Pages' is the very shape that failed in job 20261014-082328-g6vy.

steps: In `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`, add the consts: DELIVERY_VERBS = [publish, deploy, share, release]; NOT_A_DELIVERY_NEXT = [of, notes, note, process, workflow, checklist, candidate, cycle]; OBSERVABLE_STATE = the phrases listed in the decisions. Add `pub fn check_outcome_state(reading: &Reading, request: &str, attempt: Option<&EarlierAttempt>) -> Result<()>` before `check_governance_coverage` or after it in the file, with the doc comment as one `///` paragraph. The paragraph names the root cause (reading acceptance turned a delivery verb into a narrow deliverable, with no check against the state the user observes), cites jobs 20261014-082328-g6vy, 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc, states the guard (capability, no question, at least one deliverable), says it reads only the request, the earlier request, the criteria and out_of_scope, says 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.', and says the replay holds a job above the declared share + 5 points unless declared 'expected N% of newly refused readings'. It returns Ok when no verb is found, when any criterion satisfies `names_observable_state`, or when an `out_of_scope` item contains the verb (lowercase substring). Otherwise it bails with: the reading was refused because the request asks to {verb} something, but no acceptance criterion names the state the user will observe when it is done; a file that exists is not that state. Add a criterion that names it, for example 'The page is reachable at <URL>' or 'The release is downloadable at <tag>', using a word such as URL, reachable, served, live at, downloadable, installable, tag, published release or visible to; or, if this job must not {verb}, name that in out_of_scope.

risks.risk: False refusals: ordinary requests that begin with 'Release', 'Share' and similar words (the 5% share is an estimate, not a measurement).
risks.mitigation: The verb must start a sentence, line or bullet. The next word may not be of, notes, note, process, workflow, checklist, candidate or cycle. An out_of_scope item naming the verb is an explicit exit. Unit and corpus cases cover mid-sentence and noun uses. The expected share (5%) is an estimate that was not measured; the replay holds above 10% and reports the share.

risks.risk: False accepts: a criterion uses a state word that does not describe a real outcome, or mid-sentence delivery verbs are missed.
risks.mitigation: The conservative list is reported in the doc comment and the decisions entry. A criterion has to name a state, and the user still reads and accepts the criteria. The check is not intended to prove the state is real, only that the reading names it. A negated use ('not reachable') is not detected; this is stated in D161.

risks.risk: A retry's request is a complaint such as 'Try again', which hides the original verb.
risks.mitigation: Scanning `attempt.request` as well as `request` makes a retry carry the original verb. The retry pair of corpus cases covers it. A retry with no attempt record or a follow-up that cites a job only by id is not covered; this is named in D161 as a gap.

risks.risk: Missed existing tests that run a delivery-verb request through the gate and now fail.
risks.mitigation: Step 4 and step 6 list each test and update it by adding one criterion naming a reachable URL; the full `cargo test --locked` is a criterion 6 demonstration. A grep for the four verbs in reading.rs tests (done: lines 7032-7054, 7131, 7237, 7248) found these cases only; the 7237 and 7248 tests are unaffected (decline, question, empty, governance first).

risks.risk: The 5% share could be too low against the real history, which a planner cannot see (records/ is absent).
risks.mitigation: The plan does not run the replay. It adds a source test asserting the declaration text, and the replay runs at verification as it does for the earlier reading checks (design_existing_code, code_survey). If the share is above 10%, the job is held and the reason is reported to the user.
